title: Weekend rains leave Nuevo Laredo with a clean sheet: no rescues, no stranded cars
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's Civil Protection and Fire Department reported a clean sheet — saldo blanco — after the weekend's rain, with about 67 millimeters falling and no stranded vehicles or rain-related emergency calls.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's Civil Protection and Fire Department reported a clean sheet — saldo blanco — after the weekend's rain, with about 67 millimeters falling and no stranded vehicles or rain-related emergency calls.

The department said it monitored weather conditions and the city's main trouble spots through the weekend. Storm drains, cattle guards and natural and man-made drainage channels operated at 100 percent, helping move the accumulated water out of the streets, and runoff from several sectors drained without incident.

Crews kept watch on the waterways that usually cause the most worry: Canal Concordia, Voluntad 4, Lomas del Río, Pancho Villa, Cavazos Lerma and the El Coyote arroyo. The city's main bridges and avenues stayed passable throughout the weekend.

With cool weather continuing and the chance of more rain, Civil Protection is asking residents to keep drains, rooftops and patios clear so water does not accumulate. The department will continue monitoring conditions and urges residents to stay informed through official channels and report any risk.

To request help from Civil Protection and Firefighters, residents can call 867 712 8911, 867 712 2124 or 867 712 3030. The city's service center, CIGA, can be reached at 072, and emergencies go to 911.

Sources: Oficina de Corresponsales, Nov. 9, 2026; NubeTam, Nov. 9, 2026.
